items.t: Popkum is a small unincorporated community in the Fraser Valley Regional District (FVRD) Electoral Area D, east of the City of Chilliwack, near Rosedale and Bridal Falls; the FVRD is the local government for its electoral areas, providing planning and development approvals, building inspection and bylaw enforcement among its electoral-area services, while member municipalities govern themselves — so City of Chilliwack zoning does not apply in Popkum. The guide page, citing the FVRD's Electoral Area D Housing Needs Report (March 2021), describes Area D — which includes Popkum and Bridal Falls — as bounded by the Fraser River to the northwest, Electoral Area B to the north and east, Electoral Area E to the south and the City of Chilliwack to the west, and describes Popkum as a suburban residential neighbourhood closely affiliated with Chilliwack. An official boundary for the Popkum community itself: Not verified — the guide page states none was found.
The school on the Rosedale/Popkum/Bridal Falls side of the district is Rosedale Traditional Community School, 50850 Yale Rd, Rosedale; the guide page describes it as a kindergarten-to-grade 8 school.

The narrower confirmed position, carried from the neighbouring Bridal Falls research, is that BC Transit's Route 71 route-overview page, Trip Note B, confirms on-request trips can route to Bridal Falls and/or the Community and Cultural Recreation Centre in Agassiz.

Parks and services: Cheam Lake Wetlands Regional Park (FVRD) is a 107-hectare park of lake, marsh and forest in Electoral Area D at 53480 Elgey Road, Rosedale, where 184 different bird species have been recorded and pets and other domestic animals are not permitted, in accordance with FVRD Bylaw No. 1500, 2018. Health care: Chilliwack General Hospital, 45600 Menholm Road, Chilliwack, is the Fraser Health community hospital serving Chilliwack and nearby areas, providing 24/7 emergency and acute care. Guide-only claims recorded as site copy only, not verified pass: the Chilliwack and Agassiz library branch details (no branch in Popkum), the finding that published directories list no community/recreation centre in Popkum, and the Area D size/population figures in the page's FAQ.

items.t: FVRD plan and zoning — numbers not verified where no FVRD source was opened, stated as such: the guide page states the Popkum-Bridal Falls (Area D) Official Community Plan, FVRD Bylaw No. 1501, was adopted by the FVRD Board in January 2021, after a public hearing on December 15, 2020 — the bylaw text itself was not opened on an FVRD source pass, so the bylaw number and adoption details are not verified against the FVRD record and are not asserted here. Chilliwack's OCP and zoning bylaw numbers do NOT apply in Popkum — never borrow them across the municipal line.

ALR frame: on ALR land, the principal residence maximum is a total floor area of 500 m²; a secondary suite is permitted only when it is entirely contained within the principal residence and local bylaws permit it; and one additional detached residence is permitted without an ALC application at up to 90 m² on properties of 40 ha or less, or up to 186 m² on properties over 40 ha, subject to local bylaws. ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; Strata Property Act s.239; Agricultural Land Commission Act s.21(1)). Parcel-level ALR status for any specific Popkum property: Not verified — confirm on the ALC's ALR maps.

Manufactured-home pad rent (MHPTA), for the park product nearby: pad rent may rise at most once every 12 months, on 3 full months' notice, by no more than the yearly limit plus a proportional amount — 2026 = 2.3% plus proportional, 2027 = 2.2% plus proportional. That regime applies to pad tenancies like Mt Cheam's.

items.t: (1) In the main "Popkum questions" FAQ, the question "How do I see current Popkum listings?" appears with NO answer in the main FAQ block as read — the client-reviews block follows it instead.

Chilliwack's rules are the wrong rules here, three times over. Popkum owners plan and build under the FVRD (not City of Chilliwack zoning), pay under the rural Taxation (Rural Area) Act regime — 5% after July 2 and a further 5% after October 31 — and have no SnapStats coverage, even though mailing addresses on the feed read "Rosedale" and the community is closely affiliated with Chilliwack. A closing adjustment, zoning opinion or pricing sheet built on Chilliwack sources misstates this community on all three points.
The FVRD plan numbers for this area are carried as not verified, deliberately. Confirm the current OCP and zoning bylaw directly with the FVRD for any specific parcel.

A live development proposal is not stock — and its revised form dropped townhomes. An FVRD public notice for a Popkum major OCP amendment proposal records a March 10, 2026 public information meeting at Rosedale Traditional Community School and states the applicant's revised proposal removed all multi-family residential uses (townhomes and row homes), leaving single-family lots, secondary suites and commercial outdoor storage in the revised form described. A proposal under consideration creates no condos or townhomes to buy, and nothing from it is counted in. Popkum - Major OCP Amendment - 2026.pdf

Two opposite tenures sit minutes apart and get conflated in the same searches. At Mt Cheam Mobile Home Park, 52604 Yale Road, Rosedale, you buy a home and rent the pad (MHPTA governs, increases capped at 2.3% plus proportional for 2026 and 2.2% plus proportional for 2027, all-ages); at 53480 Bridal Falls Road you buy freehold strata land (no pad rent, SPA governs). Neither is in Popkum itself, both surface under Popkum / East Chilliwack searches, and the financing, resale and document packages are entirely different.

Cheam Lake is the area's park anchor — and pets are not permitted in it. Cheam Lake Wetlands Regional Park (107 hectares, 53480 Elgey Road, Rosedale; 184 bird species recorded) prohibits pets and other domestic animals under FVRD Bylaw No. 1500, 2018 — a practical point for a buyer choosing Popkum partly for dog-walking ground.

items.t: Jurisdiction — FVRD Electoral Area D (stated expressly): Popkum is in FVRD Electoral Area D (Popkum–Bridal Falls); the FVRD is the local government for its electoral areas, providing planning and development approvals, building inspection and bylaw enforcement among its electoral-area services, while member municipalities govern themselves — so City of Chilliwack zoning does NOT apply in Popkum, and City of Mission bylaws are likewise never borrowed.

Planning/zoning process — numbers not verified, process documented: the guide page states the Popkum-Bridal Falls (Area D) Official Community Plan, FVRD Bylaw No. 1501, was adopted by the FVRD Board in January 2021, after a public hearing on December 15, 2020 — the bylaw text itself was not opened on an FVRD source pass, so the bylaw number and adoption details are not verified against the FVRD record and are carried here as guide-page statements only. The FVRD zoning bylaw and the zone of any Popkum parcel were likewise not confirmed on an FVRD source: Not verified. Other regional districts' same-letter bylaws are a name collision, NOT citable. The process instead: confirm the parcel's plan designation and zone with the FVRD before relying on any use or building claim.

Property taxes — RURAL regime (stated expressly): Popkum is not in a city, town, district or village, so its properties are rural-area properties: the owner receives the tax notice from the Province's Surveyor of Taxes Office and pays the Province. Under the Taxation (Rural Area) Act, s.11, rural taxes are due July 2, a 5% penalty is added to any portion unpaid on July 2, and a further 5% to any portion unpaid on October 31. No municipal flat penalty applies to this ground.

Flood and hazard: the guide page states published records it read do not list an FVRD or BC document stating a flood or debris-flow hazard for the Popkum area. Parcel-level flood or hazard mapping for any Popkum property: Not verified — check site-specific hazard mapping with the FVRD before building or buying.
